speaker: Doctor
text:
I'm Dr. Agent. I see you've had sudden vertigo; have you noticed any hearing loss, tinnitus, or ringing in your ears alongside this dizziness?  
Also, did the onset happen while you were turning your head or lying down?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Did this episode occur just once, or have you experienced similar spinning sensations on multiple occasions since then? Additionally, do you have a history of high blood pressure, diabetes, or smoking?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Gastroenteritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). The brief duration (3 minutes) and lack of hearing loss make vestibular neuritis or Meniere's disease unlikely, despite the previous misdiagnosis of gastroenteritis. I recommend you perform the Dix-Hallpike maneuver; if positive, we will treat with canalith repositioning.
